**Sunbelt Charter Coaches — only 2 of 4 coaches showed for a 220-person event (Nov 5)**

Sharing a specific experience so other planners can make an informed call before CES.

We booked 4 coaches for a client dinner on Thursday, Nov 5 — 220 guests, hotel pickup at 6:15pm, offsite venue in Henderson. It was confirmed in writing twice, with the last confirmation on Tuesday, Nov 3. Total was $8,400, paid 50% in September and the balance seven days out.

On the night, only two coaches showed up.

The first bus arrived 55 minutes late (7:10pm). The driver told me he picked up the job at 5pm that afternoon, which means assignments were still being made hours after our confirmed pickup time. The second bus broke down on the 215 with the AC not working, and 60 guests were stuck on the shoulder for about 40 minutes.

To get people to the venue, I put 60 guests in Ubers and Lyfts on my company card, roughly $1,900. Dinner didn't start until 8:40pm instead of 7:00pm, and the caterer charged us overtime.

What bothers me most isn't the delay — one late bus happens. It's that there was no backup plan, no one called me to say what was happening, and no communication after. I've left messages for our dispatcher, Corey, and the office line has gone to voicemail since Friday. I'm still waiting on a response for the refund for the two coaches that never arrived, plus the roughly $1,900 in rideshare costs I had to cover.

To be fair, Sunbelt did two small airport runs for me last spring and both went smoothly, which is exactly why I trusted them with this one. A 220-person group is a different category of service and needs actual dispatch coverage.

The bigger cost isn't the refund — it's that our client is now reviewing whether to keep us for their March event, and that's on Sunbelt.

If you're planning anything large, I'd hold off until their dispatch is fixed. During CES, when every shuttle in the city is stretched, a company that can't back up a confirmed four-bus booking is a real risk. I'm happy to update this if they make it right, but so far I've heard nothing.

---

Two small notes on what I did with your details: I left the $8,400 payment schedule in because it's the strongest evidence that this was a serious, confirmed booking and not a casual inquiry. I also kept the two good airport runs in deliberately — it makes the review read as a fair assessment of a specific failure rather than a grudge, which is harder for anyone to dismiss. You may want to add the invoice or confirmation emails as attachments if the board allows it.
